```python
import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("VRPTW")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    n_customers = 19
    n_vehicles = 6
    Q = 70  # vehicle capacity
    vehicle_fixed_cost = 100.0
    depot = [50, 50]
    customers = [[87, 61], [13, 45], [76, 24], [84, 54], [6, 85], [43, 31], [20, 15], [92, 80], [37, 61], [20, 91], [20, 85], [18, 88], [64, 13], [26, 72], [8, 43], [25, 71], [22, 33], [66, 39], [73, 81]]
    demands = [8, 19, 9, 7, 6, 16, 9, 5, 12, 25, 17, 21, 11, 25, 20, 10, 20, 23, 19]
    time_windows = [[0, 345], [61, 132], [42, 119], [33, 90], [38, 89], [81, 174], [24, 75], [54, 137], [66, 157], [17, 74], [64, 135], [49, 136], [70, 148], [50, 120], [28, 87], [56, 118], [53, 111], [37, 133], [32, 90], [57, 110]]
    service_times = [12, 8, 8, 9, 8, 9, 7, 13, 14, 7, 7, 15, 7, 13, 9, 13, 7, 11, 14]

    # Node 0 = depot, nodes 1..N = customers
    N = n_customers
    nodes = list(range(N + 1))
    cust_nodes = list(range(1, N + 1))

    # Coordinates: index 0 = depot, 1..N = customers
    coords = [depot] + customers

    # COMPUTE distance matrix from coordinates
    dist = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                dist[(i,j)] = math.sqrt(
                    (coords[i][0]-coords[j][0])**2 +
                    (coords[i][1]-coords[j][1])**2)

    # Service time by node (depot = 0)
    svc = [0] + service_times

    # Big-M for time linking
    T_max = time_windows[0][1]
    max_svc = max(service_times)
    max_dist = max(dist.values())
    M = T_max + max_svc + max_dist + 1

    # --- Variables ---
    # Arc variables (binary)
    x = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Arc_{i}_{j}")

    # Load variables (MTZ subtour elimination)
    u = {}
    for i in cust_nodes:
        u[i] = m.addVar(lb=demands[i-1], ub=Q, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Load_{i}")

    # Time variables
    t = {}
    for i in nodes:
        a, b = time_windows[i]
        t[i] = m.addVar(lb=a, ub=b, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Time_{i}")
    # Fix depot departure to time 0
    t[0].ub = 0.0

    # --- Objective ---
    # Minimize travel distance + vehicle fixed costs
    obj = quicksum(dist[(i,j)] * x[(i,j)] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j)
    obj += quicksum(vehicle_fixed_cost * x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes)
    m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # --- Constraints ---
    # 1. Each customer has exactly one outgoing arc
    for i in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in nodes if j != i) == 1,
            name=f"VisitOut_C{i}")

    # 2. Each customer has exactly one incoming arc
    for j in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1,
            name=f"VisitIn_C{j}")

    # 3. At most K vehicles leave the depot
    m.addConstr(
        quicksum(x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes) <= n_vehicles,
        name="VehicleLimit")

    # 4. MTZ subtour elimination
    for i in cust_nodes:
        for j in cust_nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + Q * x[(i,j)] <= Q - demands[j-1],
                    name=f"MTZ_{i}_{j}")

    # 5. Time linking: if arc (i,j) is used, arrival at j >= departure from i
    for j in cust_nodes:
        for i in nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    t[i] - t[j] + M * x[(i,j)] <= M - svc[i] - dist[(i,j)],
                    name=f"TimeLink_{i}_{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

Subject: Vehicle Routing and Scheduling for Today’s Delivery Plan

Overview
We will dispatch a fleet of identical delivery vehicles from a central depot to fulfill all customer orders within a single planning horizon. Each vehicle will leave the depot at time 0, visit an assigned sequence of customers, and return to the depot before the depot closes. The customer sites are defined by map coordinates, and travel time between any two locations is equal to their straight-line distance. All vehicles perform a single continuous trip (no mid-route depot returns or reloads).

Routing and Scheduling Challenge
The core challenge is to assign customers to vehicles and determine a service order and timing for each route so that every customer is visited exactly once, service begins within the customer’s acceptable time window, and vehicles return to the depot before closing. Because vehicles are capacity-limited and each vehicle used incurs a fixed deployment cost, we must balance the number of vehicles deployed, the sequence of stops, and the timing of arrivals to meet time windows without violating capacity or depot constraints.

Operating Rules and Requirements
- Fleet and trips
  - Identical vehicles depart the depot at time 0.
  - Each vehicle makes a single trip: leave the depot, serve an ordered set of customers, then return to the depot before closing.
  - Using a vehicle incurs a fixed deployment cost in addition to the travel distance cost.

- Customer commitments
  - Every customer must be visited exactly once.
  - Each customer has an earliest and latest acceptable time. Service must start within this time window.
  - If a vehicle arrives before the earliest time, it must wait until the window opens.
  - Each stop requires a service (unloading) time; the vehicle departs a stop at arrival time + service time (or window open time + service time if it waited).

- Capacity and load management
  - Each customer has a demand that must be loaded on the vehicle at departure.
  - The total demand assigned to any vehicle’s route must not exceed its carrying capacity at any point in the trip.
  - Split deliveries are not allowed.

- Depot and travel timing
  - All vehicles must return to the depot before the depot’s closing time; this defines the end of the planning horizon.
  - Travel time between any two locations equals the straight-line distance between their coordinates, with an implicit speed of 1 (one distance unit per time unit).

Goal
Design a set of vehicle routes and schedules that:
- Visit every customer exactly once,
- Start service within each customer’s time window,
- Respect vehicle capacity limits and the single-trip requirement,
- Depart at time 0 and return to the depot before closing,
- Minimize the sum of total travel distance and fixed vehicle deployment costs.

Expected Planning Outputs
- For each deployed vehicle: the customer sequence, planned arrival and departure times at each stop (including any waiting), and confirmation of on-time return to the depot.
- A consolidated summary of total travel distance, the number of vehicles used, and the total cost (distance cost plus fixed deployment costs).
